title: PODCAST | The Spillover: Why Won’t Europe Do More for Ukraine? | Council on Foreign Relations
gist: CFR Spillover hosts Sebastian Mallaby and Rebecca Patterson interview Anne Applebaum, who argues Ukraine has achieved a drone-driven stalemate at the front and is degrading Russian refining (30-40% offline), while Russia pivots to terrorizing civilians and a sabotage campaign across Europe aimed at fracturing European support. All support for Ukraine now comes from Europe; the binding constraint is political (pro-Russian populism, US unreliability, Europeans hoarding weapons for themselves) rather than fiscal/interest-rate pressure.

insights.claim: Anne Applebaum says Ukraine has built its own long-range strike system independent of US technology and intelligence, enabling strikes deep into Russia including refineries in Moscow.
insights.speaker: Rebecca Patterson
insights.so_what: Ukraine's strike capacity no longer hinges on US policy, reducing leverage of Washington over the war's trajectory.
insights.quote: They have built their own long-range strike system, which is not dependent on the U.S. or American technology or, as I understand it, even American intelligence.
insights.locator: They have built their own long-range

insights.claim: Ukraine's medium-range drones have created a 20-30 km no-go strip along the front where a Russian soldier's life expectancy is roughly 30 minutes, so Russia cannot move the front line.
insights.speaker: Rebecca Patterson
insights.so_what: A drone-enforced kill zone implies a frozen front and shifts the war to economic and civilian attrition.
insights.quote: The life expectancy of a Russian soldier who enters into this zone is something like 30 minutes.
insights.locator: So the Ukrainians can see everything

insights.claim: Applebaum estimates 30-40% of Russian refining capacity is out, and beyond a threshold of maybe 50% Russia would be unable to move troops due to diesel shortages.
insights.speaker: Rebecca Patterson
insights.so_what: Refinery outages tighten Russian product exports and diesel markets; a ~50% threshold is a watchable tipping point for Russian logistics.
